reviewMethod: Manual review of the three World Bank WDI metadata glossary pages, API documentation, and Natural Earth terms. Collection dates are maintained separately.
license: CC BY 4.0 with World Bank dataset terms; retain World Bank and original-provider attribution. The three indicator glossary records label these series CC BY 4.0; check exceptions when adding data.

indicators.name: Individuals using the Internet (% of population)
indicators.definition: People who used the Internet from any location in the last three months, using any supported device.
indicators.methodology: The indicator aggregates survey responses on individual Internet use. Country methods and estimates can vary; consult the original metadata and country notes.
indicators.limitation: Internet use does not measure connection affordability, speed, device access, accessibility, or ability to participate in online education.
indicators.question: How widely is the Internet used?
indicators.context: A starting point for investigating digital access, rather than a direct measure of access to learning.

indicators.name: Access to electricity (% of population)
indicators.provider: World Bank / ESMAP — SDG 7.1.1 Electrification Dataset
indicators.definition: The share of the population with access to electricity.
indicators.methodology: The Global Electrification Database combines household surveys, censuses, and other sources. Modelled estimates may be included; access is different from the quality of service.
indicators.limitation: Access does not establish reliable, affordable, or continuous electricity supply, or whether a learner has a usable device.
indicators.question: How widely is electricity accessible?
indicators.context: A basic infrastructure condition to investigate alongside local reliability and device availability.

indicators.name: Lower secondary completion rate, total (% of relevant age group)
indicators.definition: A proxy based on new entrants to the final grade of lower secondary education, regardless of age, divided by the population at the intended entrance age for that grade.
indicators.methodology: UIS compiles education survey data mapped to ISCED. This gross intake proxy assumes entrants complete the final grade and does not account for final-year dropout. The reference year is the year the school year ends.
indicators.limitation: It can exceed 100% because entrants may be older or younger than the intended age. It is not a direct measure of learning quality, individual ability, or adult readiness for online education.
indicators.question: What does the education completion proxy show?
indicators.context: One aspect of education pathways, to investigate with local and disaggregated evidence.
